# Give Workstation tour playback and chrome an optional owner

## Context

Workspace currently owns TourRunner construction, cuePromise/cueReceipts/cueErrors/cueSettlements/progressPromise, startTour/runTourSpec, beat/settlement callbacks and the tour toolbar. This is a distinct playback lifecycle surrounding the gesture executors.

This is a leaf of the dedicated Workstation consumer-refactoring epic. The shared outcome is a ≤1,000-total-line composition entrypoint with working ordinary docking and optional scripted demos.

## The Problem

The named responsibility currently lives on `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs`, coupling its state, caller surface and teardown to the root. This leaf removes that responsibility and updates its actual callers in the same PR; it does not create a forwarding method for every moved member.

## The Architectural Reality

Placement pre-flight: toolbar/view files under apps/workstation/view match FeedPane/ScalePane and WorkspaceController's ordinary view/controller families. The optional tour-toolbar ViewController is the stateful playback owner, using the inherited core.Base lifecycle and the existing TourRunner; gesture implementations remain in the tour domain. Preserve the App Worker owner and render-target split; no new engine surface is prescribed.

## The Fix

Introduce a dedicated declarative tour-toolbar view whose optional, actually attached ViewController owns playback. That controller owns the TourRunner, cue/progress queues and driver instances, publishes caption/progress/start/error/completion state through the existing root Provider, and uses getReference for paint settlement. Do not add a separate helper owner plus forwarding controller. Reuse TourRunner's existing stepSettlement callback. Normal boot can show a lightweight start control with a string handler resolved through the existing controller hierarchy; load/construct the playback controller and runtime only when activated. Update the existing buttons and witnesses to this owner, leaving no shadow tour queues on Workspace.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Playback and cue settlement | Workspace onTourBeat/settleTourStep/onTourStepSettled/startTour/runTourSpec; TourRunner.stepSettlement | One owner sequences cues, projections and progress with existing semantics | Failure retains diagnostic receipt and usable workspace | Owner/toolbar JSDoc | Existing dense-tour and cross-zone cue receipts |
| Optional activation | Existing Start dense tour UI and ordinary Viewport boot | Lightweight normal boot; runtime created on explicit activation | Disposed runtime cannot continue playback | App README activation note | Fresh boot without runtime, then successful activation |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Playback methods and cue/progress state leave Workspace; the new owner contains the executed logic and owns TourRunner plus its drivers.
- [ ] Normal docking, panes, save/restore and theme controls work without a TourRunner, InteractionService or gesture-driver instance created for the demo; driver implementations are loaded only on activation.
- [ ] The existing start/caption/pip/complete/error experience and step-settlement ordering survive; repeated starts do not duplicate runners, queues or listeners.
- [ ] Destroy/cancel settles owned pending work and removes playback listeners without destroying borrowed workspace state or stores.
- [ ] Use the existing unit suite and selected dense-tour/film/cross-zone witnesses with exact-head receipts; no weakened timing, identity or geometry assertions. Each new module stays below 2,000 total source lines. Record the Workspace entrypoint's before/after total physical line count and each moved owner's count in the PR.

## Out of Scope

New screenplay content, scheduler or pointer machinery; native policy changes; moving ordinary docking controls behind the tour activation gate.

## Avoided Traps

No giant helper or copied post-setup factory descriptors; no shadow Group/document registry; no feature removal or weakened assertions to meet the size bar. Preserve explicit creator/borrower cleanup. Existing defects require baseline attribution rather than a false green.

## Decision Record impact

Aligned with ADR 0029; preserves existing engine operation, Group, projection and native-window contracts. Any required engine-contract change must be separately authorized and linked before this leaf merges.
